source.title: The Curious Case of Benign Memorization
source.authors: Sotiris Anagnostidis; Gregor Bachmann; Lorenzo Noci; Thomas Hofmann

record.file_problem: The complete paper text is present; no garbling or truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether memorization can coexist with useful performance on clean held-out data, using nearest-neighbor probing of embeddings from networks trained on random labels rather than evaluating the network's own clean-label test accuracy.
record.gate_note: Rows record nearest-neighbor probing of clean labels after training with random labels, comparing data augmentation with no augmentation. The paper also reports linear probing and several figure-only results, but these do not directly measure V1's held-out accuracy for the trained network.
record.test_reason: Section 3 explicitly reports its own replication of the random-label arm of V1: zero training error with no generalization to random or clean test labels without augmentation. The extracted rows instead measure clean-label probing of frozen embeddings, which does not test V1's classifier-accuracy comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: augmentation enables perfect random-label fitting alongside useful encoder features, with memorization concentrated in the projector. Their capacity-based mechanism is an interpretation and hypothesis, not a complete demonstrated explanation.
record.recipe_differences: Studies training on random labels with data augmentation and evaluates learned embeddings by K-NN probing; the cited Zhang et al. random-label experiments excluded data augmentation. The paper also uses mixup augmentations.
record.method_sensitivity: Data augmentation changes the result: without augmentation, clean-label K-NN probing is below initialization; with standard augmentation it rises well above initialization. The study also reports effects of augmentation count, strength, and label-noise level, often in figures.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label training with augmentation produces useful clean-label embedding probes while fitting the original random training labels perfectly; without augmentation, probe accuracy falls below initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label memorization can coexist with useful representations, as measured by a separate classifier supplied with clean training labels; this depends on augmentation in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C reports better embedding probing with larger projectors, including beyond sizes permitting memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing projector width can improve downstream representation quality during random-label training under the tested computational budget.

record.problems: The principal clean-label outcome is nearest-neighbor probing of embeddings rather than test accuracy of the trained classifier. Main comparisons report no uncertainty estimates. Several additional results are presented only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from the reported K-NN results in Table 2. Figure-only results on layers, augmentation count and strength, noise level, and invariance were not extracted as numerical rows.

untested.parts: The matched comparison showing the naturally labeled classifier's own above-chance held-out accuracy is not reported as such; the clean-training columns also report probes. The original named architectures are not evaluated.
No width sweep of the specified classifiers trained to convergence with their own test errors; Figure 8 varies a projector under a fixed computational budget and evaluates embedding probes.
No convolutional versus fully connected classifier comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap comparison.
No removal and retraining experiment using memorization-ranked examples.

missing.what: The authors' own no-augmentation replication reports zero random-label training error and no generalization to either random or clean test labels. Extract these separately from K-NN probing; classifier test percentages are not supplied in the prose.
missing.locator: Section 3, Random labels and memorization; Table 2 caption for perfect unaugmented training accuracy

record.verdict_notes: Remove both probe-based V1 verdicts in the record. Poor probing without augmentation does not limit V1, and strong probing with augmentation does not challenge chance-level random-label classifier generalization: the probes receive clean training labels. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the trained classifier's own held-out accuracy on natural labels or the random-label classifier's held-out accuracy; its clean-label result is nearest-neighbor probing of learned embeddings. It tests augmented ResNet18 and VGG11 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet, not the version's named small Inception, AlexNet, and MLP settings or ImageNet.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Train with random labels and standard data augmentation; probe embeddings using K-NN on clean labels.
rows.measure: K-NN probing accuracy on clean test labels (percentage)
rows.note: The paper states that all models except INIT reach perfect (unaugmented) training accuracy; the reported test measure is a K-NN probe, not the trained classifier.
rows.check: The numbers match Table 2, but clean-label K-NN probing does not measure V1's trained classifier accuracy. The augmentation recipe also includes mixup.
